title: Var=n is literally the Johnson ceiling: the SAME flat-profile equality saturates both Cauchy-Schwarz steps (F7 period variance = W-Johnson tightness)
wall: W-BGK / W-Paley: the worst-case B = max_{b!=0}||eta_b|| (non-principal Paley eigenvalue) is the open object; the 2nd moment / Var=n controls only the average and is provably blind to B.
evidence: Three exact probes on PROPER dyadic subgroups mu_n < F_q* (n=8 q=1009 beta=3.33; n=16 q=7681 beta=3.23; n=32 q=12289 beta=2.72; n=64 q=65537 beta=2.67; n << sqrt(q)). scripts/probes/_407_conn/C045_var_vs_johnson.py confirms identity (1) sum_b||eta_b||^2 = q*n exactly (avg = n), but the period spectrum is NOT flat and B/sqrt(n) GROWS 2.52->2.50->3.10->3.34->5.45 (not -> the flat value sqrt(n)). The connection's central equational claim breaks in three precise places: (P1, C045_two_flatness_directions.py) the period step it cites, 'max_b||eta_b||^2 <= sum_b = q*n', is the trivial max<=sum, NOT Cauchy-Schwarz; its equality case is a SINGLE SPIKE (all mass on one frequency), the OPPOSITE of the Johnson cauchySchwarz_eq_iff_flat equality (which is FLAT S_j). The two 'flat'/equality configurations the connection identifies are opposites. (P2, magnitude) the bound that step yields is B <= sqrt(q*n), loose by 12x-47x: B/sqrt(qn) = 0.079, 0.035, 0.030, 0.021 -> 0; and sqrt(qn)=sqrt(q)*sqrt(n) is NOT 'sqrt(q) per word' nor the 'Johnson sqrt(n) deficit' -- it is a different, vacuous object. (P3, C045_var_blind_to_B.py) avg ||eta_b||^2 (= Var = n) is a CONSERVED quantity pinned at n, while the actual B sits at fraction 0.50-0.83 of the way from sqrt(n) (flat/Salem-Zygmund/Ramanujan extremal) to n (trivial ceiling) and moves AWAY from flat as n grows -- so the same average n is compatible with the whole range B in [sqrt(n), n] and carries ZERO information about B. The genuine CS-from-moments route (cs_B from the 4th moment) is the moment-method face-3 of the open core (needs E_r(mu_n), NOT just the 2nd moment), and still overshoots true B.
honest_note: The connection has a real kernel: BOTH in-tree identities (subgroup_gaussSum_secondMoment and cauchySchwarz_eq_iff_flat) ARE second-moment statements, and each has a 'flat' extremal -- that analogy is sound and was correctly read from the two source files. What is REFUTED is the strengthening to 'one object on two faces' / 'Var=n IS the Johnson ceiling, equality exactly the flat spectrum': (a) the two equality cases point in opposite directions (Johnson flat over n COORDINATES vs period spike over q FREQUENCIES), (b) the period step quoted is max<=sum not CS and yields the wrong, vacuous magnitude sqrt(qn), and (c) Var=n is the AVERAGE (always n, never the obstruction) and is provably blind to the worst-case B that the prize needs. The thing the prize actually hinges on -- the deviation of the mu_n period spectrum from flat, i.e. B = the generalized-Paley non-principal eigenvalue -- is exactly what neither identity sees; this welds back to the BGK/Paley wall (open). This should be added to DISPROOF_LOG.md as a refuted route ('the 2nd-moment/Var=n identity is NOT the Johnson tightness equality; average is blind to B'). Probes are exact-integer for the identity sum (q*n closed form) and high-precision complex for the spectrum maxima at small n; not a Lean lemma.
